title: Equipment & trading
summary: Custom qualities, heroic stats, bags and the trading economy.
body:
Not released: The Classic raid reward candidate gives every dungeon three exclusive designs. The 14 added dungeons contribute 42 designs in two qualities; all 414 dungeon rewards become MAGIC. Fear, Hate and Sky receive lore-driven relics and equipped utility clicks. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

Quest ingredient qualities — not released

A candidate fix lets Normal-item quest requirements accept Polished, Exalted and Ascended versions of the same item. For example, Shakrn Meadowgreen in South Karana will accept an Aviak Charm of any ordinary quality plus two Star Rubies for Crafted Gauntlets. The ingredient is consumed and the quest's configured reward stays the same. The separate class-armor reward candidate below changes which reward that quest grants. Exact Normal items are used first when both are offered. Explicit quality requirements, reforging recipes and separate epic, hunt and dungeon catalogs retain their own rules. This fix still needs deployment and in-game testing.

Classic race robes — live testing

Game update 2026102203 corrects the waist gap reported on Barbarian and Half Elf robes. The correction covers male and female Half Elves, Wood Elves, Barbarians, Dwarves, Trolls, Ogres and Halflings. Close EverQuest completely, reopen the normal launcher and press Play to update. Other players also need the update to see the corrected models. Equipment eligibility and item stats remain unchanged. Native waist, dye and animation acceptance is still pending.

THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

The update uses unmodified stock ProjectEQ as an approximation of standard EverQuest, then preserves the exact researched values where available. It changes 143,332 existing tier definitions across 47,809 eligible ordinary families. Normal items, the 209 starter families, custom Hunt/dungeon rewards, augment families and quest-only epics keep their existing treatment. Families that exceed native stat limits are excluded for review.

Ascended fieldCandidate target from stock
Positive AC, HP, mana, primary stats, resists, weapon damage and HP/mana regeneration2×
Haste1.5×, rounded
Spell Damage when stock has noneHigher of 2× INT or WIS
Healing Amount when stock has none2× WIS
Accuracy when stock has noneHalf DEX, rounded upward
New heroicsQuarter of the final matching stat, rounded; Ascended only

Polished and Exalted receive one-third and two-thirds of the increase from Normal to Ascended. These intermediate formulas and extrapolation beyond the screenshots are Nightcap tuning choices. Attack and sparse utility fields use stock values unless an exact observed override applies. Existing effects, sockets, delays, equip rules, loot routes and owned items are preserved.

Live testing: Selected Ascended items now use reviewed THJ values, including reductions. Starter upgrades remain modest and comparable Normal dungeon gear is stronger. Spell Damage and Healing Amount have 750 base caps, plus earned Hunt headroom.

Browse the equipment catalog → Find a reward by slot, required level or source zone, with all four qualities grouped together.

Player trading and duplicate items

Trade formerly NO DROP and NO TRANSFER items, already-attuned gear, bags, their contents and augments. LORE restrictions are disabled, so duplicate ownership is allowed. Inventory capacity, temporary-item expiration and Pet Armor restrictions remain. Equipment eligibility still depends on your held classes and the remaining item requirements.

Polished, Exalted, and Ascended loot

Eligible dropped equipment and bags can appear in three stronger custom tiers. Their health, mana, defenses, and offensive stats scale by item family.

Ordinary eligible equipment and bags now roll 20% Polished, 5% Exalted and 1% Ascended, leaving 74% Normal when all variants exist. These chances apply per eligible item drop, not per kill. Already generated loot is not rerolled. Zone-hunt and dungeon rewards retain their separate rates.

New augments and gear in 48 Classic zones

Each eligible native enemy has a separate 0.5% chance for its zone’s augment and 0.5% chance for its new gear piece. Both can drop together, and ordinary loot remains. Each family averages one drop per 200 eligible kills; there is no guaranteed drop or pity counter. Once a family drops, its quality is Base 60%, Polished 30%, Exalted 8%, or Ascension 2%. Cities, hubs, pets, merchants and summoned copies do not provide these rewards. See the zone reward list.

Six armor locations for heroic augments

Eligible Base and tiered head, arms, hands, chest, legs and feet armor gains one type-22 socket, preserving existing sockets. Zone augments add stats and heroic attributes; item level requirements still apply. At level 50, every two effective heroic INT from these socketed augments allows one more point of item Spell Damage, up to +30; heroic WIS does the same for Healing Amount. With the current 750 cap, either can reach 780. Extra cap room only helps when you have enough of the actual bonus.

Upgrade matching rewards

#zoneforge uses three Base copies for one Polished reward, then four Polished for one Exalted or four Exalted for one Ascension. Artisan Veyra’s reusable Reforging Box also upgrades four identical Polished or Exalted copies, including eligible ordinary tiered gear. The box also accepts three identical eligible Normal/Base copies for Polished; higher recipes stay at four. Read Item upgrades for inputs, restrictions and the two distinct top-tier names.

Heroic stats on Ascended equipment

Ascended gear and Ascended epics add heroic stats on top of their improved base stats. This describes the existing equipment tiers; the new zone rewards have their own heroic stats at each quality.

Gear bonuses for casters and healers

Eligible direct damage spells and procs add effective Spell Damage once. Each ordinary DoT tick adds half the effective bonus, rounded down, independent of duration. Healing Amount retains percentage healing and its existing HoT distribution. Each item-bonus total has a 750 base cap; eligible Hunt augments can raise it to 780 at level 50 when enough actual bonus is equipped. Clients also gain 0.1% per heroic INT on direct damage and per heroic WIS on direct healing; DoTs and HoTs do not gain this heroic multiplier. The separate Bard area-DoT route retains its native behavior.

More room for core stats

The normal core-stat cap is raised to 425, with heroic stat effects handled separately.

Ascended summoned equipment

Eligible summoned gear becomes Ascended when a matching version exists. The supported Paladin and Cleric summoned-hammer families have zero merchant resale value at every quality, including items you already own. Summoning does not bypass spell or item-level requirements.

More room in your bags

Buy bags up to 40 slots, with base prices from 10 to 7,500 platinum. Merchant price adjustments and each bag’s capacity and contents restrictions still apply. Free trading does not reduce expensive bag purchase prices.

Better payouts for ordinary loot

Boosted merchant payouts remain in place for ordinary loot. Formerly NO DROP items use the fixed one-platinum payout below instead of those price modifiers.

One platinum for formerly NO DROP items

Ordinary merchants and #sellall pay exactly 1 platinum per physical item from the eligible formerly NO DROP pool. Five stack units pay 5 platinum; a charged object pays 1 platinum total. Purchase prices have a one-platinum floor. Merchant previews can differ from actual payment. Zone-hunt rewards, dungeon rewards and the supported divine summoned-hammer families have no merchant resale value.

Bulk selling from the command or merchant window

Use #sellall to sell eligible carried items without targeting a merchant, or use the merchant window’s Sell All button. Containers, food, drink, spell reagents and casting focus items are kept. Zero-value items, including zone rewards and the supported divine summoned hammers, are skipped. Sales are immediate and can include valuable gear. Bank anything you want to keep first.

Winged Helm of the Dawn

A custom Paladin helmet with an installed appearance for visual testing. No acquisition quest or loot source has been added yet.

Wear gear for your whole build

Ordinary equipment recognizes all held classes. Class-matching wearable items and augments allow all playable races; deity, level, slot, weapon and augment restrictions remain. See equipment eligibility.

Dungeon completion rewards

Raid and Grind dungeons have 24 shared reward designs and three exclusive Raid designs for each of the seven released dungeons. Grind grants Normal; Raid grants Polished or Ascended. These permanent, tradeable, non-lore items have zero merchant resale and no existing forging recipe. Their bags have up to ten slots and 100% weight reduction.

Item click reuse

Items without an explicit shared reuse group keep their own cooldowns without locking unrelated abilities. Copies of the same item share reuse; explicitly grouped items still share their group. Existing saved waits retain their expiry. See the cooldown update.

Reviewed Ascended values

Supported numeric fields on 131 Ascended items now follow inspected THJ Legendary references. These families use per-item values rather than one universal multiplier. Some values are lower than before; original effects and existing sockets remain.

Selected Ascended reference values
ItemValues
Heavy Yttrium Chestplate150 AC; 250 HP and mana; 40 Spell Damage and Healing Amount
Blood Cord70 AC; 200 HP and mana; 40 STA and 10 heroic STA; 40 Spell Damage and Healing Amount
Talisman of Vah Kerrath250 HP and mana; 8 to each heroic attribute; 30 Spell Damage and Healing Amount

Starter upgrades and dungeon progression

Approved starter families use smaller steps: Bronze chest armor has 6, 7, 8 and 9 AC across Normal, Polished, Exalted and Ascended. Bronze Long Sword has 4, 5, 6 and 7 damage at fixed delay 32. Cultural armor is excluded from this retuning. Comparable Normal dungeon rewards remain stronger.

Earned melee and pet equipment

Selected items gain sympathetic healing, combat procs or received-healing support. Healing, Runic and Hastened Fragments of Truth and Bloodfrenzy Core have earned boss routes; later-era bosses still require their normal access. Bloodfrenzy Core is a power-source item, while the original Bloodfrenzy remains a weapon. New sockets do not bypass augment compatibility.

Ascended class-armor quest rewards

Crafted, Lambent, Darkforge, Ivy Etched and Totemic quests now grant existing Ascended versions of their 37 reviewed armor rewards. Substantial class-armor quests qualify even when repeatable; cheap/basic hand-ins stay excluded. Materials and quest requirements remain. Already-owned armor is not automatically converted. Scope and live testing.
